cards.b: Red, yellow and blue on the traditional paint wheel; they cannot be mixed from other colours.
Orange, green and purple, made by mixing two primaries.
Made by mixing a primary with a neighbouring secondary, e.g. blue-green.
Opposite each other on the wheel (blue/orange, red/green, yellow/purple). High contrast.
Neighbours on the wheel, e.g. yellow, yellow-green, green. Calm and harmonious.
Tint: hue plus white. Shade: hue plus black.
How pure or vivid a colour is. Mixing in its complement lowers it.
Warm (red, orange, yellow) advance and feel energetic; cool (blue, green, purple) recede and feel calm.
Paint onto wet paper so colours bleed softly. Good for skies and atmosphere.
Paint onto dry paper for crisp edges and detail.
A thin transparent layer of paint over a dry layer to deepen colour.
Thickly applied paint, often with a palette knife, so marks stand out.
Opaque, matt, water-based; can be rewetted and reworked; good for flat colour.
Fast-drying and permanent when dry; opaque or glazed; good for layers, texture and bold colour.
Transparent; work light to dark; the paper provides the white; hard to correct.

gaps.s: Red, yellow and blue are the ___ colours.
A hue with white added is a ___.
Paint applied thickly with a knife is called ___.
A thin transparent layer over a dry layer is a ___.
Colours next to each other on the wheel are ___.
The medium that is opaque, matt and can be rewetted is ___.
In watercolour, white is made by leaving the ___ unpainted.

short.q: Explain how to avoid muddy colours.
short.model: Mix no more than three colours, clean the brush between mixes, use complementaries to darken instead of black, and avoid overworking wet paint.

short.q: Compare acrylic and watercolour in two ways.
short.model: Acrylic is opaque and permanent when dry and can be built thickly; watercolour is transparent, works light to dark and uses the paper as white.

short.q: How can complementary colours create a focal point?
short.model: Placing a small area of one colour against a large area of its opposite makes it look brighter and draws the eye.
points: opposite colour makes it stand out

short.q: Describe the effect of an analogous palette.
short.model: It gives a calm, harmonious, unified look because the colours are neighbours on the wheel.

short.q: How do you show AO2 when choosing a medium?
short.model: Test the same subject in several media, review them against your intention and select one with a written or visual reason.
